implementation: Encrypted individual records in system SQLite; only changed rows are encoded/encrypted/written.
FULL durable SQLite COMMIT precedes in-memory publication and delivery ACK.
Legacy snapshot migrates atomically; encrypted v1 recovery copy preserved. New database creation is atomic too.
Registered startup and backup restoration load history off MainActor.
Unchanged UI message projections are reused; public-key hashes use a bounded cache.
Portable encrypted backups retain v1 format, never copy a live SQLite database without WAL.
Encrypted row identities with keyed opaque index values; per-row authenticated bucket and order.
Writes and checkpoints are serialized across connections, including older system SQLite versions.
Account deletion waits for background preparation; invitations arriving during startup are retained.
Production Release explicitly disables code coverage instrumentation.
Batch read receipts reuse one message index; fixed-size public PeerIDs use a bounded cache.
In-order updates and appends avoid building a full-history row index; SQL bookkeeping and UI projection caches mutate only after successful changes.
